newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse sees 96 turnover up threefold.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse sees 96 turnover up threefold.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) said on Thursday total 1996 turnover was seen exceeding 2.2 billion dinars ($428.9 million), up threefold over 1995.
Its 1995 turnover stood at 717.6 million dinars.
Some analysts said the rise in BSE turnover resulted from changes in the dinar exchange rate.
Until November 1995, the dinar was fixed to the German mark at par. After a 70 percent devaluation, the dinar rate was changed to 3.3.
BSE general manager Pava Zecevic said total turnover stood at 2.167 billion dinars to December 25.

The central bank short-term bonds and forward contracts selling agricultural produce, issued by Serbia's Commodity Reserve agency, accounted for roughly 60 percent of the total, BSE general manager Pava Zecevic told reporters.
The remainder was generated in the commercial paper and treasury bill segments, she said.
Zecevic said the structure of turnover became unfavourable over the year due to lower trade in the central bank bonds which generated nearly 70 percent of last year's turnover.
"Declining activity in those securities resulted from worsening liquidity of the Yugoslav banking system. But overall, in a situation like this, we can be satisfied with those results," she added.
Zecevic said she hoped for a better performance in 1997.

"We enter the new year with completed infrastructure of the financial market, more banks are expected to join the bourse either as brokers or as dealers and there are some signals that there will be few more brokerages registered.
"But a really encouraging thing is that we are currently negotiating with several banks, planning to list their shares on BSE maybe as early as in January," she said.

The Belgrade bourse has not traded any equities over past two years. Two shares -- by Investbanka and Sintelon -- were listed but never traded and earlier this year withdrawn. Activity remains focused on short-term securities.
